title: Will not compromise national interest for PM's India visit: Bangladesh
content:
Bangladesh says Tarique Rahman’s India visit will happen only after progress in bilateral talks, stressing national interests

Bangladesh has said there is “no rush” for Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to visit India and stressed that Dhaka would not compromise its national interests while seeking a positive relationship with New Delhi. State minister for foreign affairs Humayun Kabir said Rahman’s visit would take place at an appropriate time after sufficient progress was made in bilateral discussions, state-run BSS news agency reported. “If we reach an agreement based on our national interests tomorrow, we can go next week, or the week after. There is no rush here,” news agency PTI quoted Kabir saying. The remarks came after external affairs minister S Jaishankar said ties between India and Bangladesh should serve the mutual interests of both countries.

title: SIR ordeal: ‘Was envoy for India in 3 countries, but tough to prove citizenship’
content: Based in Punjab with journalistic experience of over two decades, Navjeevan Gopal is a senior journalist reporting on crucial issues such as drugs, crime, gangsters, terror and other security issues in the border state. The Punjab Police is one of his core beats. Currently an assistant editor with The Times of India in Punjab Bureau, he comes with a vast experience of over 18 years in The Indian Express, the national daily known for its investigative journalism. Gopal had started his career in journalism with the Hindustan Times as a contributor, gradually moving to The Indian Express and thereafter TOI. He also covers Punjab’s politics with his area of interests being the 104-year-old party Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). He also extensively reported on Sikh diaspora settled across the globe.
